Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

Job Description

Position Summary:

The Associate Chemist prepares and analyzes environmental samples using standard analytical techniques according to approved scientific methodology in compliance with Eurofins Environment Testing Quality Assurance programs and standard operating procedures (SOPs). This position can be a physical job that may require standing for long periods, working with organic solvents, laboratory glassware and specialized equipment.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Performs routine lab tasks that provide experience and familiarization with methods, practices, and programs. These include:
Preparation of samples using standard techniques
Performing chemical analysis using standard techniques
Evaluation and quantification of data
Recording and reporting data and any unusual test occurrences to the supervisor
Performing routine instrument maintenance

Competency in complex instrumentation instrument specific software (training is provided)
Responsible for keeping personal training documentation (training records, IDOC/DOC) current and accurate
Responsible for timely completion of assigned/scheduled QC samples (MDL, LOD/LOQ, PT)
As required, documents NCMs for projects with quality issues
Understands and utilizes backlog reports to manage personal workload
Works under close supervision using routine and standard methods
Regular attendance and punctuality
Responsible for general housekeeping in work area
Proficient with IDOCs, for assigned methods carried out in the department
Responsible for performing job functions in compliance with Eurofins Environment health and safety and quality assurance standards
Demonstrates and promotes the company vision
Inventories and stocks laboratory supplies
Washes and inventories glassware
Purges analyzed samples
Assists in other areas of laboratory when needed
Additional duties as assigned

Follow and learn appropriate protocols in one or more of the following disciplines. This role will focus on PFAS Analysis and LC/MS.

Organic preparation
Metals preparation and analysis
PFAS sample preparation
HRMS sample preparation
Gas Chromatography
Liquid Chromatography
Mass Spectrometry
Radio Chemistry
Wet Chemistry
High Resolution preparation and analysis
Low Resolution preparation and analysis

This Position Is Open On The Following Shifts

M-F, 1st shift, 7am-3:30pm. Training will be the same hours.
Tues-Sat, 2nd Shift 3pm-11:30pm. Training will be M-F 7am - 3:30pm.

Qualifications

Basic Minimum Qualifications

BS or BA in Chemistry or related field, Associate Degree, or 2 years of related laboratory experience in lieu of degree.
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English.
Authorization to work in the United States without restriction or sponsorship

Ideal Candidates Will Have

Previous experience with PFAS and/or LC/MS
Previous experience in a lab or production setting
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
Able to interpret written materials and communicate findings effectively.
Demonstrated ability to identify issues, analyze root causes, and propose practical solutions.
Applies critical thinking to evaluate options and make decisions.
Effective collaboration skills to contribute to team goals and support department productivity goals
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage priorities and meet deadlines.
Effectively balances multiple tasks while maintaining accuracy.
Comfortable using mathematical formulas and tools to perform calculations and analyze data.
Consistently delivers high-quality work within established timelines and specifications.
Able to work independently, following written or verbal instructions with minimal oversight.
Strong interpersonal skills; able to coordinate tasks and communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.

Additional Information

Pay rate: $18-19/hour + 10% differential for 2nd shift.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

The benefits package offered will vary based on the employee’s full-time or part-time regular status.

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialized and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralized and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

Position Summary:

Position Summary & Responsibilities:

This posting is for an Environmental Specialist position in the Federal Facilities Unit at KDHE. The Federal Facilities Unit is within the Bureau of Environmental Remediation and specializes in supervising and facilitating the cleanup of contaminated sites associated with activities of the federal government. We oversee active military installations within Kansas, as well as Formerly Used Defense Sites (FUDS) across the state. The Environmental Specialist position acts as a project manager for assigned sites, and is tasked with reviewing technical reports, authoring decision documents, conducting field oversight, upkeeping the administrative record, and partnering with other Federal and State Agencies to ensure that remediation projects are conducted in accordance with applicable regulations, policies, and best practices.

Serves as KDHE project manager for environmentally contaminated sites or other assigned projects that are variously complex in nature within the Federal Facilities Program. Projects are part of Federal Facilities and Formerly Used Defense Sites (FUDS). Reviews and evaluates technical work plans, proposals and reports for completeness, accuracy, and technical adequacy. Includes analysis and interpretation of environmental and other technical data to identify and develop solutions to project-specific environmental problems. Evaluates investigative, monitoring, and general remedial progress to ensure projects are completed within a time frame deemed adequate by KDHE, established by State or Federal law, and established through Department of Defense and Site Memorandum of Agreement (DSMOA). Interacts with consultants and the public to review, present and negotiate all aspects of project management. Coordinates project management with other applicable bureaus and programs within the agency and other governmental or regulatory entities. Communicates all aspects of project specific management with the Unit Manager. Communication with the Section Chief and Bureau Director may also be required as appropriate.The employee may be temporarily assigned to assist other programs or projects in completing other duties. (Project Management)

Reviews and/or evaluates groundwater, soil, sediment, and/or surface water quality sampling programs to assure field procedures and other requirements are effectively performed in accordance with the approved Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) including project-specific field sampling plan, QAPP, quality management plans, work plan, and applicable state and federal guidance and policies. Follows all appropriate agency/bureau/section/state/federal program guidance, policies, and procedures. Performs site visits for the purpose of oversight of inspections, field investigations and remediation. Company Description

APPOINTMENT TYPE:
Temporary Exempt: This position is excluded by the Charter from the competitive Civil Service examination process and shall serve at the discretion of the Appointing Officer. The duration of the appointment shall not exceed 36 months.

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission:
To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision:
We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site at https://www.sfpuc.org/about-us/careers-sfpuc

Why Join Us?

This role offers a unique opportunity to help build and scale up critical water quality initiatives, combining technical analysis, project coordination, and field operations to protect public health across San Francisco and regional water systems. If you are passionate about water quality, regulatory compliance, large-scale infrastructure programs, and building efficient operational processes, we encourage you to apply!

Job Description

Project Name:
Hazard Assessment Program

Project Description:

Under the State of California’s new cross-connection control regulations, the SFPUC must review all service connections (~180,000+) to properties in San Francisco, as well as the eight other water systems under SFPUC’s control, to evaluate potential hazards to the public drinking water distribution system arising from activities on user premises. In addition, the new regulations require the installation of backflow prevention assemblies on about 4,200 fire service connections. SFPUC has submitted a plan to the State Water Resources Control Board with deadlines for completing hazard assessments by 2049, ensuring backflow prevention assemblies on all dedicated fire services by 2044.

Position Summary

Are you a technical professional looking to make a direct impact on public health and water safety on a massive scale? We are seeking a dynamic Utility Specialist to serve as the Technical Program Coordinator for our Water Quality Cross Connection Control (CCC) Program under the direction of the Hazard Assessments Program Manager.

In this vital role, you will contribute to the implementation of SFPUC Cross-Connection Control Program inline with new regulatory requirements established by the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) through the Cross Connection Control Policy Handbook (CCCPH).

You will help shape a high-profile, multi-decade program by developing tracking systems, operational processes, coordinating complex field logistics, and partnering with internal teams, contractors, and external stakeholders across multiple program areas including Hazard Assessments, Fire services upgrades and Regional Compliance.

Work Location:
1657 Rollins Road, Burlingame, CA, 94010

Schedule:
Full-time, Monday – Friday

This position requires a valid driver’s license.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Program Implementation & Compliance: Develop and implement coordination protocols, workflows, and documentation processes for the CCC Program in compliance with SWRCB CCCPH requirements.
Systems & Data Management: Establish tracking systems, dashboards, and reporting templates to monitor inspections, costs, schedules, and compliance metrics.
Research & Analysis: Conduct research using internal databases, GIS systems, spreadsheets, field reports, and photos to compile baseline data on service connection characteristics and assess cross-connection hazards.
Cross-Functional Coordination: Coordinate daily program activities with field staff, contractors, customers, and other City departments, serving as a liaison to ensure smooth communication, scheduling, and execution.
Contractor & Consultant Oversight: Coordinate with contractors and consultants to ensure field activities align with approved scopes of work, schedules, and Cross Connection Control program requirements.
Reporting & Continuous Improvement: Prepare program reports, dashboards, and documentation for Program Manager review, highlighting trends, risks, and lessons learned while developing procedures, reference materials, and recommendations to improve program effectiveness.
Field Engagement: Conduct field coordination and site visits (as needed) to support hazard assessments, inspection activities, and validation of program data.
Technical Support: Provide technical support for Hazard Assessment Program initiatives, including compliance studies, analytical tasks, and administrative support. Performs other project-related duties as assigned.

What We’re Looking For (Desirable Qualifications)

We are seeking analytical, highly organized professionals who bring technical expertise and strong stakeholder management skills to our team. Ideal candidates possess:

Technical or Scientific Degree: A baccalaureate degree in a technical or scientific field, such as Civil, Environmental, Mechanical, or Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, Physical Science, or a closely related discipline.
Compliance & Program Management Experience: Demonstrated experience coordinating or managing compliance, regulatory, technical, or project/program-related work within a water utility, similar utility environment, public agency, or closely related regulatory setting.
Project Coordination Mastery: Strong organizational and project coordination skills, including managing multiple priorities, tracking activities, monitoring progress, and maintaining accurate records .
Stakeholder Engagement: Proven experience communicating and working collaboratively with diverse stakeholders, including field staff, contractors, regulators and customers.
Technical & Analytical Acumen: Ability to conduct regulatory research, analyze technical and operational information, and support the development and implementation of policies, procedures and program improvements .

Under the State of California’s new cross-connection control regulations, the SFPUC must review all service connections (~180,000+) to properties in San Francisco, as well as the eight other water systems under SFPUC’s control, to evaluate potential hazards to the public drinking water distribution system arising from activities on user premises. The WBG Chief Risk Officer (CRO) Vice Presidency is the core unit responsible for Group-wide institutional risk oversight, including establishment and monitoring adherence to risk policies and guidelines and risk assessment and reporting to the Board and executive management. Its mission is to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in a financially sustainable manner. The VPU assists management with identifying and managing Group-wide cross-cutting risks, enhancing risk response decisions, reducing financial and operational surprises and losses, seizing opportunities and improving deployment of capital. The WBG CRO Vice Presidency includes the IBRD/IDA, IFC, and MIGA risk teams and covers a wide range of financial and non-financial risks.

To enhance accountability and credibility, the World Bank Group (WBG) has established an independent second line of environmental and social risk oversight within its Chief Risk Officer (CRO) function called CROES. While operational teams at the World Bank, IFC, and MIGA are responsible for designing and implementing projects in accordance with E&S policies, the newly formed E&S Risk Department—led by the WBG Global Director for Environment and Social Risk—oversees, monitors, and evaluates E&S risk and performance.

CROES seeks a seasoned, dynamic, and motivated Senior Environmental or Social Specialist with strong technical judgment and substantial experience in social risk management. The selected candidate will support independent second-line oversight of operations and portfolios across the World Bank Group, with balanced thematic coverage of environmental and social aspects, such as pollution prevention, labor and working conditions; land acquisition, biodiversity conservation, resettlement and livelihood restoration; stakeholder engagement and grievance mechanisms. Independent E&S Risk Oversight

Assess the adequacy of E&S risk identification, assessment, mitigation measures, monitoring arrangements, and escalation pathways proposed by operational teams, while maintaining independence from first-line responsibilities.
Provide independent technical opinions on E&S risk categorization, application of relevant E&S policies and standards, adequacy of mitigation measures, institutional capacity, and implementation readiness.
Review project documentation, E&S assessments and management plans, stakeholder engagement arrangements, advisory products, and relevant legal commitments from an independent E&S risk perspective.

Lead or support quality assurance reviews of selected operations, assessing the quality of E&S due diligence, management of stakeholder impacts, feasibility of mitigation measures, and capacity to meet applicable E&S requirements.

Portfolio Monitoring and Analytics

Conduct thematic and sector-specific portfolio reviews to identify systemic E&S risk trends, recurring implementation challenges, and emerging risk patterns.
Analyze E&S risk events and lessons learned to strengthen institutional risk practices and contribute to enterprise-level reporting and integrated risk dashboards for senior management and governance committees.
Recommend improvements to E&S risk management practices based on portfolio experience, independent assessments, and international good practices.

Mentor junior staff and provide technical guidance to specialists, associates, and analysts working on E&S risk reviews.

Successful candidates will be interested in ecology, wildlife biology, soil science, hydrology, environmental policy, geography, botany, earth sciences, natural resources stewardship, and water resource management. Environmental sampling while following appropriate sample integrity and chain-of-custody procedures
Sample coordination with appropriate laboratory for sample analysis
Site visits to document other environmental compliance and associated reporting

Job Description

Johnson, Mirmiran & Thompson is a dynamic, 100% employee-owned consulting firm with more than 2,800 professionals, providing a full range of multidisciplinary engineering, architecture, information technology, and related services to public agencies and private clients throughout the United States. JMT is currently ranked #45 on Engineering News-Record’s list of the Top 500 Design Firms.

JMT is an employee-owned firm where people work together, support one another, and take pride in delivering meaningful results for our clients and communities. Our collaborative culture brings together the accountability of ownership, the technical depth of a multidisciplinary team, and the shared commitment to help our people and projects succeed.

What You Will Help Us Build:
If you are a Senior Water Resources leader who enjoys developing people, shaping team culture, and helping a practice grow with purpose, this role offers an opportunity to make a visible impact. JMT is expanding its Water Resources leadership capacity across Texas and Colorado, and we are looking for a leader who can strengthen operations, mentor technical staff, support project delivery, and help position the practice for continued regional growth.

Why JMT:
At JMT, you will join an employee-owned firm where technical leadership, collaboration, and accountability are part of how we work. Our Water Resources practice is delivering a growing portfolio of transportation, municipal, drainage, floodplain, stormwater, and water quality projects, and we are looking for someone who wants to help guide that work while investing in the people behind it. This is a strong fit for a leader who values trust, mentorship, client service, and the chance to help build something lasting in key regional markets.

Position summary:
The Water Resources Section Head will lead staff, operations, client engagement, and delivery oversight for a growing regional practice. This position is responsible for developing people, managing workload and financial performance, supporting business development, and providing senior technical guidance across drainage, stormwater, floodplain, H&H, and water quality services.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Lead, mentor, and develop Water Resources staff, including performance management, staffing needs, and career growth
Manage section operations, including workload planning, utilization, budgets, backlog, staffing forecasts, and financial performance
Support strategic growth planning for the Water Resources practice in coordination with regional and office leadership
Strengthen client relationships and support business development with transportation, municipal, county, flood control, and stormwater clients
Lead or support pursuit strategy, proposals, interviews, and client presentations
Provide senior technical leadership and quality oversight for drainage, hydrologic and hydraulic, stormwater, floodplain, and water quality projects
Advise project managers and technical staff on complex delivery, risk management, staffing, and client-service decisions
Promote collaboration across offices and disciplines to deliver consistent, high-quality solutions

Nonessential Functions And Responsibilities

Perform other related duties as assigned

Required Skills

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, water resources engineering, or a related field from an accredited program
Texas Professional Engineer license or the ability to obtain licensure within 6 months of hire
10+ years of progressively responsible water resources experience
Experience in TxDOT drainage design for TxDOT transportation projects (or other DOTs)
Familiar with TxDOT Design Standards and the TxDOT Drainage Manual
Experience with Open Roads Designer production and Open Roads Drainage and Utilities modeling
Experience with HEC-RAS 1D and 2D roadway drainage applications and stormwater management design
Experience in HEC-HMS software
Demonstrated experience leading, supervising, mentoring, or developing technical staff
Experience managing operations, project delivery, financial performance, workload planning, and client expectations
Experience with business development, proposal development, client coordination, and pursuit strategy
Strong leadership, communication, organizational, and decision-making skills

Qualifications Preferred

Experience as responsible drainage task lead for complex H&H schematic and PS&E projects involving modeling, design, and drainage reports
Established client relationships in Texas, Colorado, or similar regional markets
2-D HEC-RAS, SWMM, ARC-GIS experience
Experience with TxDOT, municipal, county, flood control, transportation, or stormwater clients
Technical background in drainage design, H&H modeling, floodplain studies, stormwater management, and water quality compliance
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams across multiple offices or regions
Certified Floodplain Manager certification or other relevant technical certification

Work is performed within a general office environment. Work is generally sedentary in nature, but may require occasional standing and walking. Lighting and temperature are adequate and there are no hazardous or unpleasant conditions caused by noise, dust, etc. within the office environment.
